title: From TikTok to Tradition: A New Generation Is Looking Back to the Roots of the West
author: Hirsi Ali, Ayaan
summary: This article argues that the West is experiencing a crisis of identity rooted in the severing of people from their cultural inheritance — their history, faith, and tradition — and that a rising generation is beginning to look beyond digital culture toward permanence and roots. Using Erling Haaland as a case study — a global football star who wore a cross necklace, whose national team used twelfth-century church symbols, and who spent over £134,000 on a medieval Norwegian Christian manuscript — the article argues that the desire for roots has not disappeared but has been suppressed and is re-emerging. It contends that Christianity remains central to understanding Western civilisation: its art, architecture, philosophy, laws, and moral language of human dignity all flow from that inheritance. The article argues that recovering this inheritance is not a religious requirement but a historical and civilizational necessity — a civilisation cannot preserve what it refuses to remember.
points: It shaped Europe's art, architecture, philosophy, laws and institutions, and its influence endures in the moral language of human dignity, charity, and the sanctity of life that pervades Western culture.

The West is experiencing a crisis of identity — after decades in which the connection between people and their cultural inheritance has steadily weakened, many young adults are discovering that modern life alone cannot answer deeper questions of meaning, belonging, and purpose.

A civilisation cannot preserve what it refuses to remember — the answer is not to retreat from modernity, but to recognise that tradition provides the foundations on which a society understands itself.

Haaland reportedly spent more than 134,000 pounds acquiring a rare medieval manuscript documenting Norway's Christianisation and its early Christian kings, which he later donated to a public library in his hometown.
Progress is frequently defined as moving beyond religion, national memory, and historical identity rather than building on them — the result is a growing cultural amnesia among the young.
quotes: It shaped Europe’s art, architecture, philosophy, laws and institutions and its influence endures - from the great cathedrals that define European cities to the moral language of human dignity and charity that continues to shape public and private moral life.

After decades in which the connection between people and their cultural inheritance has steadily weakened, many young adults are discovering that modern life alone cannot answer deeper questions of meaning, belonging, and purpose.

Rather than dismissing this desire for rootedness, we should engage confidently with our history—bringing the wisdom, beauty and truth of the Christian traditions that shaped the West into conversation with the present.

The answer is not to retreat from modernity, but to recognize that tradition provides the foundations on which a society understands itself, navigates the present, and moves confidently into the future.
The result is a growing cultural amnesia: societies enjoy the achievements of the Christian West even as they forget the beliefs and institutions that made those achievements possible .
At just 25, he seems to embody modern culture where global fame, commercial branding, mass sports entertainment and the relentless visibility of social media converge.
The West’s renewal will not come through nostalgia, but through a confident recovery of the ideas, institutions, and beliefs that enabled it to flourish.
